targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS running FROM experiments WHERE status = 'running'
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT schedule_id)::int AS schedules FROM experiments WHERE status = 'running'

SELECT COALESCE(MAX(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - last_seen))), 9999)::float AS gap_s FROM (SELECT chassis_id, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM telemetry WHERE time > now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes' GROUP BY chassis_id) per_chassis
SELECT COALESCE(COUNT(*), 0)::int AS critical_24h FROM alerts WHERE severity = 'critical' AND created_at > now() - INTERVAL '24 hours'

panels.title: Per-chassis state (all 16)
panels.description: One row per chassis. The grid is rendered via generate_series so empty chassis still appear; counts come from a per-status FILTER aggregate over experiments. Schedule shows the alphabetically-first running schedule on the chassis (in practice soaks enrol the whole bench under one schedule, so this is single-valued — multiple schedules running on one chassis is an unusual state worth noticing). Max cycle is MAX(cycle_index)+1 over completed experiment_steps for running experiments only — i.e. the high-water mark of the *current* run, not the bench's lifetime.

targets.rawSql: WITH chassis(id) AS (SELECT generate_series(1, 16)::smallint), counts AS (SELECT chassis_id, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='running')::int AS running, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='pending')::int AS pending, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='failed')::int AS failed, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='completed')::int AS completed FROM experiments GROUP BY chassis_id), sched AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (chassis_id) chassis_id, schedule_id FROM experiments WHERE status='running' ORDER BY chassis_id, schedule_id), maxcycle AS (SELECT e.chassis_id, COALESCE(MAX(es.cycle_index)+1, 0)::int AS max_cycle FROM experiments e LEFT JOIN experiment_steps es ON es.experiment_id = e.id AND es.state='completed' WHERE e.status='running' GROUP BY e.chassis_id), alert_counts AS (SELECT chassis_id, COUNT(*)::int AS alerts_24h FROM alerts WHERE created_at > now() - INTERVAL '24 hours' GROUP BY chassis_id) SELECT c.id AS chassis, CASE WHEN c.id BETWEEN 1 AND 8 THEN 'A (25 °C)' ELSE 'B (45 °C)' END AS chamber, COALESCE(s.schedule_id, '—') AS schedule, COALESCE(co.running, 0) AS running, COALESCE(co.pending, 0) AS pending, COALESCE(co.failed, 0) AS failed, COALESCE(co.completed, 0) AS completed, COALESCE(mc.max_cycle, 0) AS max_cycle, COALESCE(ac.alerts_24h, 0) AS alerts_24h FROM chassis c LEFT JOIN counts co ON co.chassis_id = c.id LEFT JOIN sched s ON s.chassis_id = c.id LEFT JOIN maxcycle mc ON mc.chassis_id = c.id LEFT JOIN alert_counts ac ON ac.chassis_id = c.id ORDER BY c.id

panels.title: Chamber A — cell temperature spread (chassis 1–8)
panels.description: Min/avg/max temperature_c across all channels in chamber A, time-bucketed at 30 s. Useful for spotting cells running hotter than peers under the same setpoint, and for confirming the chamber tracked its setpoint after a perturbation. The setpoint itself comes from .env (CHAMBER_A_SETPOINT_C, default 25 °C).

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket('30s', time) AS time, MIN(temperature_c) AS min_c, AVG(temperature_c) AS avg_c, MAX(temperature_c) AS max_c FROM telemetry WHERE chassis_id BETWEEN 1 AND 8 AND $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Chamber B — cell temperature spread (chassis 9–16)
panels.description: Min/avg/max temperature_c across all channels in chamber B, time-bucketed at 30 s. Setpoint is 45 °C by default (CHAMBER_B_SETPOINT_C in .env).

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket('30s', time) AS time, MIN(temperature_c) AS min_c, AVG(temperature_c) AS avg_c, MAX(temperature_c) AS max_c FROM telemetry WHERE chassis_id BETWEEN 9 AND 16 AND $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
